sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: You're listening to our second episode of Short Stories all about what may be the original designed object, the trail.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听我们的第二期“短篇故事”，这一期我们要聊聊可能是有史以来最早的设计产物——小径。

sentences.en: If you haven't heard the first episode yet, you should totally go back and listen to it.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没听过第一期，一定要回去听听。

sentences.en: It's a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣。

sentences.en: We're going to kick off this second episode with another conversation with author and trail expert Robert Moore.
sentences.zh: 第二期节目，我们先从与作家兼小径专家罗伯特·摩尔的另一段对话开始。

sentences.en: Robert wrote an excellent book called On Trails.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特写了一本非常棒的书，叫《论小径》。

sentences.en: I cannot recommend it highly enough.
sentences.zh: 我强烈推荐这本书。

sentences.en: If you've listened to the previous episode, you heard him explore the origins of trails and the way they're shaped by culture.
sentences.zh: 如果你听过上一期，就会听到他探讨小径的起源以及它们是如何被文化塑造的。

sentences.en: Today, Robert Moore is back to talk about his firsthand experience hiking and learning about one of the longest, most iconic trails in America.
sentences.zh: 今天，罗伯特·摩尔再次做客，分享他徒步穿越美国最长、最具标志性的小径之一的亲身经历，并讲述他从中获得的感悟。

sentences.en: So, Robert, your book begins with you talking about this huge challenge of hiking the Appalachian Trail, otherwise known as the AT.
sentences.zh: 那么，罗伯特，你的书开头就提到了你挑战徒步阿巴拉契亚小径（即AT）的艰巨任务。

sentences.en: Can you describe what the AT is and why it's such a massive undertaking to hike it?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下AT是什么，以及为什么徒步走完它是一项如此浩大的工程吗？

sentences.en: The Appalachian Trail is a roughly 2,000-mile path that basically follows the spine in the Appalachian Mountains.
sentences.zh: 阿巴拉契亚小径是一条全长约2000英里的路径，基本上沿着阿巴拉契亚山脉的脊线延伸。

sentences.en: So, it goes from Georgia to Maine, takes about three to six months to walk.
sentences.zh: 它从佐治亚州一直延伸到缅因州，走完全程大约需要三到六个月。

sentences.en: I did it in about five.
sentences.zh: 我用了大约五个月。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's five months of continuous hiking on a trail that follows a very rough route.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是五个月不间断的徒步，而且这条小径的路线非常崎岖。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of other hiking trails nowadays have been graded for horses so that they will never go above a certain incline.
sentences.zh: 如今很多徒步小径为了方便马匹通行都经过了平整，坡度不会超过一定限度。

sentences.en: The Appalachian Trail is much older than that.
sentences.zh: 但阿巴拉契亚小径的历史要久远得多。

sentences.en: It's America's oldest, very long trail.
sentences.zh: 它是美国最古老的超长距离小径。

sentences.en: And so, even though the mountains of the Appalachians are not as high as what you'd find in Colorado or California, it's just really arduous on a day-to-day basis.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管阿巴拉契亚山脉不像科罗拉多州或加利福尼亚州的山脉那样高耸，但每天的徒步都非常艰苦。

sentences.en: And I think for that reason, it's become a kind of American pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 我认为正因如此，它已经成为了一种美国式的朝圣之旅。

sentences.en: And you write in your book that the Appalachian Trail, like, it really started as this radical idea.
sentences.zh: 你在书中写道，阿巴拉契亚小径最初是一个非常激进的想法。

sentences.en: It was the first really long trail in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它是美国第一条真正意义上的长距离小径。

sentences.en: But it also has a lot of, like, philosophy and high-minded sort of notions about its existence.
sentences.zh: 但它背后也蕴含着许多哲学思想和崇高的理念。

sentences.en: Could you talk about the origins of the trail itself?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这条小径本身的起源吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the person who came up with the Appalachian Trail is a guy by the name of Benton Mackay.
sentences.zh: 当然，提出阿巴拉契亚小径构想的人叫本顿·麦凯。

sentences.en: And he had a dream of this wilderness space that would mirror the industrial beltway of the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 他梦想着建立一片荒野空间，与东海岸的工业环路相呼应。

sentences.en: And so it would be a place where the workers of the East Coast could escape to go up into the mountains, kind of refresh their spirits.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，东海岸的工人们就能逃离城市，走进山林，让心灵得到休憩。

sentences.en: And so, oddly, his original notion was not that people would be walking the entire trail in one go.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，他最初的构想并不是让人一次性走完全程。

sentences.en: That wasn't really something that was on his mind.
sentences.zh: 那根本不在他的考虑范围内。

sentences.en: He was seeing it as a way of connecting a variety of recreation centers, even a kind of sanatoria, work farms,
sentences.zh: 他将其视为连接各种休闲中心、甚至是疗养院和劳动农场的一种方式，

sentences.en: all of these outdoor sources of mental and physical health that he wanted to run all the way up the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 他希望这些户外资源能沿着东海岸一路延伸，为人们提供身心健康保障。

sentences.en: And the funny thing that happened was people loved the idea of the trail and not so much the rest of that other stuff.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，人们爱上了这条小径本身，却对其他那些配套设施没那么感兴趣。

sentences.en: So that stuff kind of withered away.
sentences.zh: 所以那些东西逐渐被遗忘了。

sentences.en: And what was left was this continuous line that people still to this day follow in a way that Benton Mackay had never intended.
sentences.zh: 最后留下的，就是这条人们至今仍在追随的连续线路，这完全超出了本顿·麦凯最初的设想。

sentences.en: And why do you think it didn't take off in that way?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么它没有按照他预想的那样发展？

sentences.en: I don't think Mackay properly anticipated how the culture of the Appalachian Trail would evolve.
sentences.zh: 我不认为麦凯充分预见到阿巴拉契亚小径的文化会如何演变。

sentences.en: I don't think he knew how popular long-distance hiking would become.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他知道长距离徒步会变得如此受欢迎。

sentences.en: And I don't think he knew how this air of heroism or sort of epic nature of the Appalachian Trail would congeal in the American imagination.
sentences.zh: 我也不认为他预料到这种英雄主义色彩或阿巴拉契亚小径的史诗感会在美国人的想象中凝聚成形。

sentences.en: I don't think he could have known that until a guy by the name of Earl Schaefer went and hiked the entire trail in one go.
sentences.zh: 直到一个叫厄尔·谢弗的人一口气走完了整条小径，这一切才真正发生。

sentences.en: When Earl Schaefer did that, people didn't even believe him.
sentences.zh: 当厄尔·谢弗完成壮举时，人们甚至不相信他。

sentences.en: He had to prove that he'd done it using photographs and his diary.
sentences.zh: 他不得不拿出照片和日记来证明自己确实走完了。

sentences.en: And so I think that Benton Mackay was actually in an odd way looking at the Appalachian Trail in a way that's very similar to how we currently look at wilderness,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，本顿·麦凯看待阿巴拉契亚小径的方式，与我们今天看待荒野的方式非常相似，

sentences.en: which is as a kind of source of mental and physical health, almost in a medicinal way, but also in a utopian way,
sentences.zh: 即将其视为一种身心健康的源泉，几乎具有某种药用价值，同时也带有一种乌托邦色彩，

sentences.en: a place where we could go to form community and to improve the civic spirit.
sentences.zh: 一个我们可以去建立社区、提升公民精神的地方。

sentences.en: That is something that the American form of wilderness travel has not really worried itself with.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是美国式荒野旅行真正关注的东西。

sentences.en: What we've worried about is going out as individuals into the wilderness, proving our mettle,
sentences.zh: 我们关注的是作为个体走进荒野，证明自己的勇气，

sentences.en: having sublime experiences of these beautiful mountains and forests.
sentences.zh: 在这些美丽的山峦和森林中获得崇高的体验。

sentences.en: And that is what the hiking aspect of the Appalachian Trail provided.
sentences.zh: 而这正是阿巴拉契亚小径的徒步属性所提供的。

sentences.en: So Earl Schaefer was the first person to hike the whole like original AT in one season.
sentences.zh: 所以厄尔·谢弗是第一个在一个季节内走完原始AT全程的人。

sentences.en: And he wrote, like, I almost wish the trail really was endless, that no one could ever hike its length.
sentences.zh: 他写道：“我甚至希望这条小径真的是无止境的，永远没有人能走完它。”

sentences.en: And what is that desire?
sentences.zh: 这种渴望源于什么？

sentences.en: You know, like, I think a lot of people think of trails as maybe getting from one place to another.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人认为小径只是从一个地方到另一个地方的通道。

sentences.en: But there seems to be this alternate desire to extend and extend and extend and never have them end.
sentences.zh: 但似乎还有一种想要不断延伸、永无止境的替代性渴望。

sentences.en: Well, a funny thing happens when you finish the Appalachian Trail, which is you feel kind of sad.
sentences.zh: 当你走完阿巴拉契亚小径时，会发生一件有趣的事，那就是你会感到一种失落。

sentences.en: You know, you think that it's going to be this joyous moment.
sentences.zh: 你本以为那会是一个充满喜悦的时刻。

sentences.en: And as I was approaching Katahdin, I remember every day I would have the thought,
sentences.zh: 但我接近卡塔丁山时，记得每天我都会想：

sentences.en: oh, what if I twist my ankle?
sentences.zh: “万一我扭伤了脚踝怎么办？”

sentences.en: What if I fall and I can't hike anymore?
sentences.zh: “万一我摔倒了，再也走不动了怎么办？”

sentences.en: And I would knock on wood.
sentences.zh: 于是我会敲敲木头祈求好运。

sentences.en: You know, thankfully, there's a lot of wood around on the Appalachian Trail.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，阿巴拉契亚小径上到处都是木头。

sentences.en: But I was doing this multiple times a day, literally knocking on wood multiple times a day,
sentences.zh: 但我每天都要做很多次，真的，每天敲好几次木头，

sentences.en: thinking I just want to get to the end.
sentences.zh: 心里想着我只想走到终点。

sentences.en: I just want to get to the end because I don't want to fall short of my goal.
sentences.zh: 我只想走到终点，因为我不想让目标半途而废。

sentences.en: And then when you get there, you realize that, you know, there's no more trail.
sentences.zh: 而当你真正到达终点时，你会意识到，没有路了。

sentences.en: You've come to the end.
sentences.zh: 你已经走到了尽头。

sentences.en: And there's a sadness.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一种悲伤。

sentences.en: And I think anyone who's read a really great book knows that feeling where you get to the last page
sentences.zh: 我想任何读过好书的人都知道那种感觉，当你读到最后一页时，

sentences.en: and you think, I wish it kept going.
sentences.zh: 你会想：我真希望它能继续下去。

sentences.en: And so there are people who do all sorts of things to try to extend that experience.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人会想尽办法去延续那种体验。

sentences.en: They'll walk from Georgia to Maine and they'll turn around and go back to Georgia.
sentences.zh: 他们会从佐治亚州走到缅因州，然后再掉头走回佐治亚州。

sentences.en: Or they'll walk the Appalachian Trail every year.
sentences.zh: 或者他们每年都会走一遍阿巴拉契亚小径。

sentences.en: It's like we want to be able to continue on the pilgrimage without it ending because it is such a beautiful experience.
sentences.zh: 就像我们希望这场朝圣之旅永不结束，因为它是一段如此美好的经历。

sentences.en: So after you walk the entire length of the Appalachian Trail, it's 2,181 miles.
sentences.zh: 在你走完阿巴拉契亚小径的全程后，那是2181英里。

sentences.en: You yourself decided that you wanted to extend that experience and you went on to walk something called the International Appalachian Trail.
sentences.zh: 你自己决定要延续这种体验，于是去走了所谓的“国际阿巴拉契亚小径”。

sentences.en: So what is the International Appalachian Trail?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是国际阿巴拉契亚小径？

sentences.en: Basically, a guy named Dick Anderson, who lived up in Maine,
sentences.zh: 基本上，一个住在缅因州的叫迪克·安德森的人，

sentences.en: was looking at maps one day and he realized that the logic of the Appalachian Trail is that it follows the Appalachian Mountains.
sentences.zh: 有一天在看地图时意识到，阿巴拉契亚小径的逻辑是它沿着阿巴拉契亚山脉延伸。

sentences.en: And yet the Appalachian Mountains don't end at Mount Katahdin.
sentences.zh: 然而阿巴拉契亚山脉并没有在卡塔丁山结束。

sentences.en: The Appalachian Mountains keep going up through Canada.
sentences.zh: 阿巴拉契亚山脉一直延伸到了加拿大。

sentences.en: So he thought, well, why not make the trail longer?
sentences.zh: 所以他想，为什么不把小径延长呢？

sentences.en: Why not just keep going as if the border doesn't exist?
sentences.zh: 为什么不假装国界不存在，继续走下去呢？

sentences.en: And in that way, it was kind of a subtly political act as well, you know, to go beyond borders, to imagine a world without borders.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这也是一种微妙的政治行为，跨越国界，想象一个没有国界的世界。

sentences.en: And so that's exactly what he did.
sentences.zh: 于是他真的这么做了。

sentences.en: He extended the trail farther and farther.
sentences.zh: 他把小径越修越长。

sentences.en: And then as soon as he got to Newfoundland, he started talking to geologists.
sentences.zh: 当他到达纽芬兰时，他开始与地质学家交谈。

sentences.en: And the geologist said to him, well, you know, the Appalachians don't really end in Newfoundland either.
sentences.zh: 地质学家告诉他：“你知道，阿巴拉契亚山脉在纽芬兰也没有结束。”

sentences.en: The Appalachians are also over in Europe because when the Appalachian Mountains formed,
sentences.zh: “阿巴拉契亚山脉也延伸到了欧洲，因为当阿巴拉契亚山脉形成时，

sentences.en: they were this kind of seam that split along the coasts of North America on the east side and then the west side of Europe.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是一道缝合线，沿着北美东海岸和欧洲西海岸裂开。”

sentences.en: And so you could continue following the Appalachian geology, if you really wanted to, down through all of Europe into North Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你真的想的话，你可以顺着阿巴拉契亚的地质结构，一路穿过欧洲到达北非。

sentences.en: And that was a really mind-blowing idea that I think Dick Anderson really liked.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常震撼的想法，我想迪克·安德森非常喜欢。

sentences.en: We are now entering this weird postmodern realm where a trail becomes a kind of text, you know, where a trail is a line on a map, a trail is an idea, a trail is a story,
sentences.zh: 我们现在进入了一个奇怪的后现代领域，小径变成了一种文本，它是地图上的一条线，是一个想法，是一个故事，

sentences.en: a trail is a collection of scientific data surrounding geology.
sentences.zh: 是围绕地质学的科学数据集合。

sentences.en: It becomes really tricky to pin down what a trail is if we're going to say that you can walk from Georgia to Morocco.
sentences.zh: 如果我们说你可以从佐治亚州一直走到摩洛哥，那么定义什么是小径就变得非常棘手。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, I think a trail is a story.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，我认为小径就是一个故事。

sentences.en: A trail is a story we tell ourselves about why we're following a certain route and why we're taking that journey.
sentences.zh: 小径是我们对自己讲述的故事，关于我们为什么要走这条路，为什么要踏上这段旅程。

sentences.en: It's what gives the journey significance in some sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这赋予了旅程意义。

sentences.en: It's a kind of myth we tell ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这是一种我们对自己讲述的神话。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: I think originally when I was walking on trails, I had this feeling that there was something slightly conformist, you know, that I should have been this pathbreaker.
sentences.zh: 我想最初我走在小径上时，总觉得这有点随波逐流，你知道，我本该是个开拓者。

sentences.en: I should have been someone breaking new ground.
sentences.zh: 我本该是个开辟新道路的人。

sentences.en: But after writing this book, after spending all this time thinking about what a trail really is, now when I walk a trail,
sentences.zh: 但在写完这本书，花时间思考小径的真正含义后，现在当我走在小径上时，

sentences.en: I see myself as taking part in this collective creation of meaning, really the making of meaning out of chaos, which is the most fundamental thing that we as human beings do.
sentences.zh: 我把自己看作是参与了这种集体意义的创造，实际上是在混乱中创造意义，这是我们人类所做的最根本的事情。

sentences.en: And there's something really, really beautiful in that.
sentences.zh: 这其中有着非常、非常美妙的东西。

sentences.en: Fans of the show who have read our book, The 99% Invisible City, co-authored by Kirk Holstead and myself, know that desire paths are trails created not by design,
sentences.zh: 读过我们与柯克·霍尔斯特德合著的《99%隐形城市》的听众都知道，欲望路径并非设计出来的，

sentences.en: but rather carved out by foot traffic as people take the path they desire and wear them in over time.
sentences.zh: 而是人们在行走时，出于自身需求踩踏出来的，随着时间推移逐渐成型。

sentences.en: Hollow ways, or simply one word, hollow ways, are desire paths gone wild, reflecting centuries or even millennia of informal use.
sentences.zh: “空心路”（Hollow ways）或者简单点说，就是野蛮生长的欲望路径，反映了几个世纪甚至几千年的非正式使用。

sentences.en: They often start as flat paths and they get carved into the ground by things going over them again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 它们通常始于平坦的小径，随着人们反复踩踏，逐渐被刻入地表。

sentences.en: Some of them are so deep, they look like long sunken half pipes.
sentences.zh: 有些深到看起来就像长长的下沉式半管。

sentences.en: Many hollow ways in places like Europe have been eroded over the centuries by a combination of foot traffic, farm animals, laden carts, and rivers of water.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲等地，许多空心路经过几个世纪的侵蚀，由行人、农场牲畜、载货马车和雨水冲刷共同形成。

sentences.en: The word hollow way itself has been traced back to the old English hollow weg, meaning sunken road.
sentences.zh: “空心路”这个词本身可以追溯到古英语“hollow weg”，意为下沉的道路。

sentences.en: Many of the actual half tunnels, though, are thought to date all the way back to Roman times.
sentences.zh: 不过，许多真正的半隧道被认为可以追溯到罗马时代。

sentences.en: They are often particularly deep in places where the ground is soft, containing high amounts of sandstone and chalk.
sentences.zh: 它们在土壤松软、含有大量砂岩和白垩的地方往往特别深。

sentences.en: Today, some hollow ways have been made more official.
sentences.zh: 如今，一些空心路已经被官方化了。

sentences.en: You can find an especially long network of these sunken paths in Germany.
sentences.zh: 你在德国可以找到一个特别长的此类下沉路径网络。

sentences.en: But across the world, many hollow ways are doing just what they've always done.
sentences.zh: 但在世界各地，许多空心路依然在发挥着它们一直以来的作用。

sentences.en: For our next trail story, 99PI producer and editor Kelly Prime recorded her journey on a bike trail that begins not in a remote forest or a mountain range,
sentences.zh: 对于下一个小径故事，99PI的制作人兼编辑凯莉·普莱姆记录了她在一条自行车道上的旅程，这条路并非始于偏远的森林或山脉，

sentences.en: but in one of the most densely populated urban centers in the country.
sentences.zh: 而是始于全国人口最稠密的城市中心之一。

sentences.en: I am on the Empire State Trail, which is this insanely long, like 750-mile-long trail you can take from New York City to Canada, from Albany to Buffalo.

sentences.en: Frequent campers and hikers probably know the word GORP.
sentences.zh: 经常露营和徒步的人可能知道“GORP”这个词。

sentences.en: But for those who don't, it's spelled G-O-R-P, all caps, and it's another name for trail mix.
sentences.zh: 但对于不知道的人，它是 G-O-R-P，全大写，是什锦干果的别称。

sentences.en: This mix of oats, nuts, chocolate, raisins, and other ingredients for on-the-go energy dates back over a century.
sentences.zh: 这种由燕麦、坚果、巧克力、葡萄干和其他配料组成的便携能量零食，历史已超过一个世纪。

sentences.en: Though the term trail mix wasn't popularized until the 1960s and 70s.

sentences.en: In other places, these mixes go by other names, too, like Scroggin in New Zealand and Australia.

sentences.en: In America, trail mix has become a useful generic.
sentences.zh: 在美国，什锦干果已经成为一个通用的称呼。

sentences.en: But GORP is still a popular shorthand for those in the know.
sentences.zh: 但对于内行来说，GORP 仍然是一个流行的简写。

sentences.en: But where did that strange name come from?

sentences.en: According to Recreational Equipment Inc., better known as REI, GORP might stand for good old raisins and peanuts.
sentences.zh: 根据 Recreational Equipment Inc.（即大家熟知的 REI）的说法，GORP 可能代表“好的老式葡萄干和花生”（good old raisins and peanuts）。

sentences.en: Or maybe granola, oats, raisins, and peanuts.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是燕麦、谷物、葡萄干和花生（granola, oats, raisins, and peanuts）。

sentences.en: But there are other possible explanations, too.
sentences.zh: 但也有其他可能的解释。

sentences.en: A century-old definition for the word GORP suggests that it meant to eat greedily.
sentences.zh: GORP 这个词一个世纪前的定义暗示它意为“贪婪地吃”。

sentences.en: And if that's true, that would make GORP a bacronym.
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，那 GORP 就是一个逆向首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: As in, an acronym created after the fact based on letters already in an existing word.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在现有单词的字母基础上，事后创造出的首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: Like almost every government program that spells something, like the CARES Act, is a bacronym.
sentences.zh: 就像几乎每个能拼出单词的政府项目，比如《CARES 法案》，都是逆向首字母缩略词。

sentences.en: Whatever the origin, the word GORP has more recently been incorporated into a portmanteau tied with another aspect of trail-centric lifestyles,
sentences.zh: 无论起源如何，GORP 这个词最近被纳入了一个合成词中，与户外生活方式的另一个方面联系在一起，

sentences.zh: 即“荒野时尚”服装。

sentences.en: And the answers were like, gnome core, Barbie core, bistro core.

sentences.en: It's like, what is going on?
sentences.zh: 这简直让人摸不着头脑。

sentences.zh: 但最早出现的风格之一，是在 2015 年，就是 GORP core。

sentences.en: And it was coined by, I believe, Jason Chen in the cut.
sentences.zh: 我相信是由《The Cut》的 Jason Chen 创造的这个词。

sentences.en: And it's this concept of looking like you're going hiking when you're not.
sentences.zh: 它的概念就是：即使你没去徒步，看起来也像要去徒步一样。

sentences.zh: 你穿着看起来应该卷起来、上面挂满登山扣的短裤。

sentences.en: And I'm sure we'll talk about this, but there's a lot more GORP in all of our lives than we might know.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们之后会聊到这个，但我们生活中其实比想象中充斥着更多的 GORP 元素。

sentences.en: And ever since, you know, over the course of especially the 20th century, but really, you know, as early as the 1850s, really ever since the rise of mass produced clothes,
